editorial:
Imagine being the first person to really master a language for storytelling, only to have the world push back against you. You get to step into the shoes of Aleksis Kivi, a man with a massive heart and a pen that could change everything. The movie feels like a cozy but sad trip back to old Finland. You will see a man who just wants to be understood and respected, but he ends up fighting a losing battle against the fancy elites of his time. It is a slow burn that focuses on the loneliness of being a genius when no one else sees your value.

What really hits home is the acting; you can feel the frustration and the sadness in every scene. The pacing is a bit slow, which might bore you if you want explosions, but it works for a character study. If you love stories about misunderstood artists, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a heartbreaking note as you see Aleksis succumb to mental illness and poverty. After being mocked by critics and ignored by the people he tried to help, he loses his grip on reality. He dies young and lonely, never knowing that he would eventually become a national hero. The final scenes show the sad gap between his miserable death and the huge fame he achieves long after he is gone.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about struggling artists and history.
